newsitem.title: CANADA: Stampeder to boost spending on heavy oil.
newsitem.headline: Stampeder to boost spending on heavy oil.

text.p: Stampeder Exploration Ltd, which earlier today announced a stock offering and a big increase in spending, planned to use the proceeds to fund stepped-up heavy oil drilling, not takeovers, Stampeder Chief Executive Jeff Tonken said on Friday.

"We are not looking at any acquisitions of any type at this time," Tonken said in a conference call. "We intend to use this money to drill the land and to exploit our significant concentrated oil and gas land base."
The company said on Friday it filed a preliminary prospectus in Canada and a registration statement in the United States for an offering of 24 million shares.

Tonken said proceeds from the issue, which at Stampeder's current share price would gross about C$140 million, would fund an increase in the company's capital spending to C$245 million from the previous budgeted amount of C$160 million.
He said the company would boost its planned drilling this year to 400 wells from 300 wells.

"We want to ensure that the company can continue to develop its properties but not be susceptible to swings in commodity prices. Nor do we want to incur excessive amounts of debt while increasing our capital expenditure program," Tonken said.
He said the company's focus on heavy oil, most of it in Saskatchewan, would give it the ability to add large, long-lasting reserves.
But the initial costs of heavy oil production, which often requires enhanced oil recovery techniques such as steam injection, were high compared to light oil, he said.
The company was already spending C$40 million developing its Kerrobert, Saskatchewan heavy oil project and expected to start steam injection in November.
But it but did not expect to reap the benefits of production until late in the first quarter of next year, he said.
He also said that Stampeder had the highest number of drilling prospects in its hopper since the company's inception five years ago.

In the conference call, Tonken reminded analysts that a C$165 million writedown resulted from a U.S. "generally accepted accounting principles" ceiling test and did not affect the company's reported Canadian results.
The U.S. GAAP writedown had to be taken last week in anticipation of the share offering, he said.
The global coordinator for Stampeder's offering is Lehman Brothers Inc and U.S. co-managers are Howard, Weil, Labouisse, Friedrichs Inc and Merrill Lynch & Co in the United States.

The Canadian syndicate, to be co-led by Griffiths McBurney & Partners and Newcrest Capital Inc, includes Peters & Co Ltd, RBC Dominion Securities Inc, CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc, Midland Walwyn Capital Inc, Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion Inc, Loewen, Ondaatje, McCutcheon Ltd and ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
Tonken said Stampeder was "well aware of the initial dilutive nature" of the stock issue and would withdraw all or part of the offering if its share price experienced a major drop.
Stampeder shares were unchanged at 6 in light volume on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday. They were down 1/8 to 4-1/4 on the New York Stock Exchange.
